newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh Uzen oil tender delayed until 1997 - minister.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh Uzen oil tender delayed until 1997 - minister.

text.p: Results of a tender to sell Kazakhstan's giant Uzen oilfield have been delayed until the first quarter of 1997, Kazakh Oil and Gas Minister Nurlan Balgimbayev said on Wednesday.
"Uzen will be privatised sometime in the first quarter of next year," he told a news conference in the former Soviet republic's capital Almaty.

He was referring to Kazakhstan's international tender to develop the field, in which Amoco Corp of the United States, Malaysia's Petronas and China National Petroleum Corp (CNPC) are the three finalists.
The result was to have been announced in November.
Balgimbayev gave no reason for the delay in selecting a winner.
Development of Uzen, Kazakhstan's second-largest oilfield after Tengiz, with estimated reserves of 150 million tonnes of oil, will cost around $1.2 billion.

Balgimbayev said investment in Uzen, located 150 km (100 miles) east of the Caspian Sea in southwest Kazakhstan, would raise the field's output of 2.5 million tonnes a year to about seven million tonnes.
